newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia property firm to double profit this year.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia property firm to double profit this year.

text.p: Indonesian property firm PT Surya Semesta Internusa, shortly to be listed, says profit and revenues will rise sharply this year over 1995.

The company, set up by several former automobile executives in 1971, expects to almost double its net profit after listing this year due to anticipated strong growth in the construction and industrial estate sectors.

"The opportunities are huge. It's still February now, but we have already received orders totalling some 70 percent of 1997 revenues target," Internusa's Vice-President Director Johannes Suriadjaya told Reuters in a recent interview.

Internusa saw its total revenues to rise to 805 billion rupiah ($337.4 million) this year from an expected 589 billion rupiah in 1996 as its net profit rose to 92 billion rupiah from 48 billion rupiah, he said.
Suriadjaya said the firm booked 20 billion rupiah net profit and 465 billion rupiah revenues in 1995.
Internusa planned to list a 20-percent stake, or 135 million shares, on the Jakarta stock exchange in late March.
Suriadjaya said he expects the firm's construction and industrial divisions to power its growth in the future.
The firm's other divisions include hotels and building materials.
Internusa said up to February it had secured orders amounting to some 81.5 percent of its expected 246 billion rupiah revenues from its industrial and real estate division this year.
"Our 1997 targets are actually very conservative considering the strong demand," Suriadjaya said.
He added that the firm had in January and February also secured orders worth around 67 percent of its whole year target of 472 billion rupiah revenues from its construction division.
Suriadjaya said Indonesia was expected to remain an attractive place for industrial estate and construction operations due to rising domestic and foreign investment.
Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said in December that domestic investment approvals were up 44.1 percent to 100.7 trillion rupiah in 1996 from 69.9 trillion rupiah in 1995.
At the same time, foreign investment approvals fell to $29.9 billion in 1996 from $39.9 billion in 1995, Sanyoto said.
Suriadjaya said Internusa was studying the possibility of forming a joint venture with a Japanese contruction firm, but he declined to name the company.
He said the firm previously had joint operations with Japanese construction companies such as Obayashi Corp and Shimizu Corp.
Suriadjaya said the Internusa planned to hold presentations in Hong Kong, Singapore and Britain in February to promote its share offering.

Internusa expects to raise between 135 billion to 168 billion rupiah from the initial public offering. Its nominal share price was 500 rupiah while the offer price was indicated between 1,000 and 1,250 rupiah per share.
Suriadjaya said the firm planned to use most of the proceeds to finance business expansion including acquiring 640 hectares of industrial land in Kerawang, West Java.
He added that firm already has a licence to develop around 1,400 hectares of industrial land in Kerawang.
